sample_unit: GenAI replies to primary care patient portal messages

links.outcome: Frequency of inaccurate content in GenAI replies to patient portal messages
links.effect: Information delivery limitations (including inaccurate content) appeared in 89/201 (44.3%) replies, outnumbering strengths (43/201, 21.4%).
links.quote: Limitations outnumbered strengths in the remaining domains of information delivery (89/201, 44.3% vs 43/201, 21.4%), information gathering (60/201, 29.9% vs 43/201, 21.4%), and responding to emotion (7/201, 8.5% vs 9/201, 4.5%).

links.outcome: Errors in AI-drafted replies to real primary care patient messages, including inappropriate or premature next steps
links.effect: 46.3% (93/201) had both strengths and limitations and 27.4% (55/201) had limitations without strengths; only 26.4% (53/201) showed strengths without limitations.
links.quote: Overall, 26.4% (53/201) of all messages displayed communication strengths without limitations, 27.4% (55/201) had limitations without strengths, and the remaining 46.3% (93/201) had both.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating GenAI patient message replies using a best-practice medical communication framework (rapport, information gathering, information delivery, next steps, emotion)

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation (content analysis by clinicians) of generative AI draft replies to real patient portal messages using a medical communication framework, but does not test a specific safeguard or deployment practice.
